Summary

`z.formatError()` and `z.treeifyError()` both throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')` when any issue path element is a name inherited from `Object.prototype`: `__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf`, etc.

These paths are reachable through `ctx.addIssue({ path: [...] })` in `.check()` / `.superRefine()`, and more generally whenever user-controlled keys end up in an issue path (for example record or dynamic-key validation). For an API that formats validation errors from untrusted input, this is a crash vector.

### Reproduction (zod 4.4.3, Node 22)

```ts
import * as z from "zod";

const schema = z.object({ data: z.string() }).superRefine((val, ctx) => {
  ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", message: "invalid value", path: ["toString"] });
});

const result = schema.safeParse({ data: "hello" });

z.treeifyError(result.error); // TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')
z.formatError(result.error);  // TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')
```

I ran this for all five names (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf`) against both functions on the published 4.4.3 build: all 10 combinations throw.

### Root cause

Both functions build their output trees on plain object literals and test node existence with truthy / nullish checks, which see inherited members.

`formatError` (`packages/zod/src/v4/core/errors.ts`):

```ts
curr[el] = curr[el] || { _errors: [] };
```

When `el` is `"toString"`, `curr[el]` is the inherited function, so the node is never created and `curr[el]._errors.push(...)` throws. When `el` is `"__proto__"`, plain assignment goes through the inherited setter and mutates the object's prototype instead of creating an own property.

`treeifyError` has the same class of bug:

```ts
curr.properties[el] ??= { errors: [] };
```

`properties["constructor"]` is not nullish, so `??=` never assigns and traversal walks into `Object.prototype` members.

### Fix

Guard node creation with an own-property check (`Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`) and create nodes with `Object.defineProperty` so that `__proto__` becomes a real own data property instead of hitting the prototype setter. This fixes the crash for all inherited names and prevents prototype mutation for `__proto__`.

I have a patch covering both `formatError` and `treeifyError` with regression tests for all five names on both functions (36 tests passing locally). Happy to open a PR.

### Related open PRs

#6083, #6139, and #6181 each address `formatError`, but as far as I can tell none of them cover `treeifyError`, which fails identically (verified on 4.4.3 as above). Filing this issue per CONTRIBUTING so there is a single reference for the full scope, with credit to those PRs for prior art on the `formatError` side.

Summary

Every CI run of `test.yml` fails at `pnpm build` since 2026-07-08, on all PRs — including docs-only changes. The cause is external: TypeScript 7.0.2 was published to npm's `latest` tag on 2026-07-08 15:55 UTC, a few hours after the last green run on `main` (06:32 UTC that day).

### Mechanism

The test job installs the matrix TypeScript before building:

```yaml
- run: pnpm add typescript@${{ matrix.typescript }} -w
- run: pnpm build
```

`zshy@0.7.2` declares `peerDependencies: { typescript: ">5.5.0" }` and resolves the workspace TypeScript. With `typescript@latest` now resolving to 7.0.2 (the Go-native compiler, which no longer ships the TS 5.x JS compiler API), zshy crashes:

```
»  Build failed: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'readFile')
ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL  zod@4.4.3 build: `zshy --project tsconfig.build.json`
```

Reproduces locally on `main` (912f0f51):

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm add typescript@latest -w   # installs 7.0.2
pnpm build                      # zshy: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'readFile')
```

Reverting to the lockfile's pinned TypeScript makes the build pass again.

Note the "TypeScript 5.5" matrix job is not independently broken — its `pnpm build` step is `cancelled` by matrix fail-fast when the `latest` job dies, so both jobs show red for one root cause.

### Possible directions

- Build with the repo's pinned TypeScript by moving `pnpm build` above the `pnpm add typescript@…` step, so the matrix TS only applies to the test/typecheck phase (which is the matrix's purpose). `pnpm test` under TS 7 may surface further issues, but they'd be the real signal rather than a toolchain crash.
- Cap the matrix at `typescript@5` until zshy supports TS 7.
- TS 7 support in zshy itself.

Happy to send a PR for the workflow reorder if that's the preferred route.

declares a schema-to-schema signature but forwards to `util.extend()`, which requires a plain shape. The call that typechecks throws at runtime, and the call that runs is a type error. There's no way to call it that satisfies both.

```ts
import * as m from "zod/mini";

const A = m.object({ a: m.string() });
const B = m.object({ b: m.string() });

m.merge(A, B);                  // typechecks; throws at runtime
m.merge(A, { b: m.string() });  // works at runtime; type error TS2353
```

On `zod@4.4.3`:

```
merge(schema, schema) THROWS: Invalid input to extend: expected a plain object
merge(schema, shape) : [ 'a', 'b' ]
```

Under `tsc --noEmit --strict` (5.9.3 and 7.0.2 agree):

```
error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties,
  and 'b' does not exist in type 'ZodMiniObject<...>'
```

## Cause

`mini/schemas.ts:921` declares only the schema-to-schema overload, so the implementation signature isn't publicly callable:

```ts
/** @deprecated Identical to `z.extend(A, B)` */
export function merge<T extends ZodMiniObject, U extends ZodMiniObject>(
  a: T,
  b: U
): ZodMiniObject<util.Extend<T["shape"], U["shape"]>, T["_zod"]["config"]>;
export function merge(schema: ZodMiniObject, shape: any): ZodMiniObject {
  return util.extend(schema, shape);
}
```

`util.extend` guards on `isPlainObject` and throws (`core/util.ts:659`).

Mini only. Classic calls `util.merge` (`classic/schemas.ts:1555`) and `A.merge(B)` works. Present since the Zod 4 commit 85928549, unchanged in 4.4.3. `mini/tests/object.test.ts` has no `merge` case.

## Two fixes, not equivalent

Correcting the overload to `(schema, shape)` matches the `@deprecated Identical to z.extend(A, B)` note above it, with no runtime change. It breaks `merge(A, B)` at compile time, but that call already throws, so the failure just surfaces earlier.

Switching the body to `util.merge` makes the advertised signature true, matches classic and Zod 3, and picks up `b`'s `catchall`. It breaks JS callers passing a plain shape, which is the form that works today. Not silently: `checks: b._zod.def.checks ?? []` (`core/util.ts:713`) is eager, so it throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'def')` at the call. Still a runtime change to a shipped API.

`merge` is deprecated and absent from `api.mdx`, so the first is the conservative read. Which would you prefer? Happy to open a PR with a test either way.

throws a `TypeError` whenever a validation issue's `path` contains a segment whose name matches a property inherited from `Object.prototype` (for example `toString`, `valueOf`, `constructor`, or `hasOwnProperty`).

Minimal reproduction:

```
import zod, { treeifyError } from 'zod';

const schema = zod.object({ toString: zod.string() });
const result = schema.safeParse({}); // success: false

if (!result.success) {
    treeifyError(result.error); // throws TypeError
}
```

The parse correctly fails: `{}.toString` resolves to the inherited `Object.prototype.toString` function, so the `toString` field is reported as `invalid_type (expected string, received function)` with `path: ["toString"]`. That part is expected. The bug is that `treeifyError` then throws while building the tree:

```
node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:113
                        curr.errors.push(mapper(issue));
                                    ^
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')
    at processError (node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:113:37)
    at treeifyError (node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:120:5)
```

Root cause:

`treeifyError` builds the tree using a plain object as a dictionary:

```
curr.properties ?? (curr.properties = {});
(_a = curr.properties)[el] ?? (_a[el] = { errors: [] });
curr = curr.properties[el];
```

When the path segment `el` is an `Object.prototype` key, `curr.properties[el]` returns the inherited member (e.g. the `toString` function) instead of `undefined`. The `??` short-circuits, so the node is never created, and `curr` is assigned the inherited function which has no `errors` array. The following `curr.errors.push(...)` then throws.
A null-prototype object (`Object.create(null)`) or a `Map` for `properties`, or an `Object.hasOwn` guard, would fix it.

  console.log("Result 4 (boolean):", JSON.stringify(result4, null, 2));
